title: How do I get started?
author: BoringApe23
selftext:
I'm not a new trader and have been investing for a few years, around six. Currently I'm using a blog and various tools to conduct week-by-week and daily market signal research to generate trend reports for myself so that I can better monitor the performance of my current stock tickers and portfolio and identify trading signals.

I'm not day trading or trading frequently. It's usually on macro signals, major market volatility, major market changes, and company news that might signal a rise or drop, but nothing frequent on a day-to-day basis. I'm interested in learning how to build a system that can manage and trade on its own autonomously. What would be the best way to go about something like this to get started?

I'm not super technical but I do have a pretty decent background in natural language processing, more for financial sentiment analysis using 401(k) and financial statements and stuff like that. I also use Fidelity for trading. I've been noticing that a lot of people have been using Bobbin Hood or something like this so I'm just wondering what people think and if there are suggestions on how to get started

comments.author: MyLinedChart
comments.body: Sounds like you already have your trading process down- nuance being trades don’t need to execute daily? You can put your existing process in to code on a daily review loop that checks if today actually needs something to happen. If not, then it just waits until the next day to check again for when that day comes when it’s time to do something

comments.author: jromeeeo145
comments.body: I totally get the frustration of trying to set up a more automated system. I spent quite a bit of time using various tools, including Fidelity and some basic scripts, but I found it tough to keep everything cohesive. I eventually turned to a platform that allowed me to track macro signals and company news more effectively, which really helped streamline my process. How are you currently identifying which signals matter most for your trades?

comments.author: Good_Character_20
comments.body: Your NLP background is the actual advantage here, so I'd build around it rather than trying to become a low-latency algo person, which your macro and news style doesn't need anyway. Autonomous really splits into two different jobs, and you're already doing the harder one by hand. Automating the research and signal side, turning filings and sentiment into a ranked view, is where your edge lives and it's a natural extension of what you already do. Automating execution is a separate and smaller step you can add later. One practical snag worth knowing early is that Fidelity doesn't offer a real retail API for automated trading, so if you want a system that actually places trades you'll probably end up adding Alpaca or Interactive Brokers alongside it, since those are the two retail-friendly programmatic brokers, and most Robinhood automation is unofficial and fragile. There are also platforms that run the whole discover-backtest-deploy loop for you if you'd rather not code it, AutoQuant being one (disclosure, I work on it), though it deploys through Alpaca rather than Fidelity. Either way I'd start by writing your current manual process down as explicit rules, backtesting that, and only automating once it holds up, because codifying what you already do beats reaching for a black-box model you can't audit.
